extracted.intended_audience: federal agency managers and OMB reviewers preparing GPRA strategic and annual performance plans (U.S. federal agencies)
extracted.subtask_short: federal strategic and annual performance plans
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing Strategic Plans and Annual Performance Plans under GPRA/A-11, including required elements, timing, submission sequence, review/clearance expectations, and performance measurement/verification practices for U.S. federal agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission statement (Strategic Plan element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic plans must include a mission statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the six required elements for an agency strategic plan. Serves as the foundation describing the agency's purpose and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: General goals and objectives (Strategic Plan element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic plans must state general goals and objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the six required elements; these articulate long-term goals the agency intends to accomplish across at least a six-year period and provide the basis for deriving annual performance goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means and strategies (Strategic Plan element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic plans must describe means and strategies for achieving goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the approaches and broad methods the agency will use to accomplish strategic goals; should connect to resources, programs, and policy tools without being a budget request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between general goals and annual performance goals (Strategic Plan element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic plans must explain the relationship between general goals and annual performance goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how long-term strategic goals translate into specific, measurable annual objectives that will be tracked and reported in performance plans and reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: External factors (Strategic Plan element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic plans must identify external factors that could affect attainment of goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss outside influences and risks (e.g., economic, legal, environmental) that may impede or facilitate program performance and how these are taken into account in planning and targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program evaluation (Strategic Plan element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic plans must address program evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe evaluation activities that will assess effectiveness of programs in meeting goals, including timing and use of evaluation results to inform strategy adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Plan coverage and revision schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic plans should cover at least a six-year period and be revised and updated every three years, with minor adjustments allowed annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans were due Sept 30 (per statute); agencies should perform periodic updates (major revision every 3 years, minor annual adjustments) and consult with Congress and stakeholders during preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation and outreach for Strategic Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation with Congress and outreach to interested or potentially affected parties (stakeholders, customers) is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide opportunity for views during plan development; transmittal materials should summarize consultation and note contrary views and contractor/consultant use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal letter requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmittal letters should summarize consultation, record contrary views, and disclose use of contractors/consultants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use transmittal letter to document interagency and Congressional consultation and to note disagreements or external assistance used in plan preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency clearance and OMB checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans must go through interagency clearance using an OMB checklist to ensure consistency across cross-cutting programs and with the President's program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB reviews drafts (e.g., summer 1996, spring 1997). Ensure consistency among agencies for programs that cut across multiple organizations; remember a strategic plan is not a budget request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managerial questions for program plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Managers should be able to answer three questions: What are you trying to achieve? How well are you doing? How do you know?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans and performance measures should be structured around these core accountability questions to focus on outcomes and measurable progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on outputs and outcomes (versus inputs)
rubrics_metrics.description: GPRA emphasizes output and outcome measures over inputs (people, dollars, process) and less emphasis on policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design performance goals to measure results (outcomes) and outputs rather than merely tracking resources or procedures; consider program entirety rather than incremental deltas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government-wide Performance Plan role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government-wide Performance Plan should show the overall relationship to the budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the government-wide plan to link agency performance goals and aggregated outcomes to budgetary priorities and resource allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Performance Report purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual Performance Reports provide accountability for results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports document progress against annual performance goals and support accountability to Congress and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Performance Plan: annual performance goals and indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual performance plans must contain annual performance goals and indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goals should be specific and linked to indicators that allow assessment of whether goals were met; examples include numeric targets (e.g., improve productivity by 10%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Performance Plan: means and strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual performance plans must describe means and strategies for achieving annual goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the programs, activities, and managerial actions that will be used during the budget year to accomplish the stated performance goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Performance Plan: verification and validation of data
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual performance plans must include a description of how data will be verified and validated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe data sources, quality controls, validation methods, and how performance information will be checked and certified for accuracy and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: program activities vs major functions; account-level linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual plans should be tied to specific program activities and budget accounts rather than agency-level aggregates or major functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance goals and indicators should align with program-level budget accounts so that achievement can be linked to funding decisions and resource use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence and timing of Annual Performance Plan submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual performance plans follow a sequence: September submission to OMB with the budget request; February submission to Congress (revised after budget decisions); September/October operating plan at agency choice (revised after appropriations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the submission calendar to ensure plans reflect budget decisions and appropriations; use operating plans to reflect final funding and operational details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative measurement form: non-qualified goals
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB-authorized alternative measurement form — 'non-qualified goal' — allows descriptive statements of satisfactory and minimally effective program performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where quantitative measurement is not feasible, agencies may use qualitative/descriptive standards that define satisfactory and minimally acceptable performance levels, with OMB authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation, disaggregation, consolidation of program activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans should address how program activities are aggregated, dis-aggregated, or consolidated for performance measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide and document whether to report at a consolidated program level or by disaggregated activities to reflect meaningful management units and avoid masking performance differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget year funding and multi-year performance funding nuances
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that budget-year funding can affect future-year performance and that current-year performance may be funded by prior appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document how funding timing affects expected performance results and account for multi-year funding effects when setting targets and reporting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of regulation and tax expenditures in achieving goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider regulatory tools and tax expenditures as means to achieve program goals and reflect their use in strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include non-appropriations policy tools (regulations, tax expenditures) in the means and strategies discussion when they materially affect program outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managerial flexibility waivers and requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and document managerial flexibility waiver requests as part of performance planning where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe any statutory or administrative waivers sought to permit alternative management or reporting approaches and explain their rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital planning linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: Address capital planning where relevant to program performance goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include capital investment plans and how capital resources support achievement of strategic and annual performance goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot projects for performance measurement and managerial flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Use pilot projects to test performance measurement approaches and managerial flexibility initiatives (e.g., FY1994-96 pilots).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document pilot objectives, scope, and results; pilots can inform broader implementation and identify appropriate measures and management flexibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB, GAO, and Congressional review mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans will be reviewed by OMB (guidance, checklists, interagency reviews), GAO (checklist, letter reports), and Congressional teams (scorecards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate reviewers' concerns; use OMB checklists and heed GAO recommendations to improve plan completeness and defensibility; prepare for Congressional oversight and scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good practice examples of goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clear, actionable goal statements (examples given: 'Improve productivity by 10 percent', 'Promote economic growth in Appalachia', 'Maintain combat forces at a high level of readiness', 'Reduce product defects', 'Eliminate errors').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer measurable, specific, and outcome-focused goals; numeric targets where possible; geographic or program-specific goals when appropriate. Examples illustrate range from quantitative to programmatic objectives.
